paper.title: EvoTest: Evolutionary Test-Time Learning for Self-Improving Agentic Systems
paper.central_claim: EvoTest evolves the whole agentic configuration (prompt, memory, hyperparameters, tool-use routines) from episode transcripts without gradients, giving faster test-time learning on J-TTL than reflection, memory, prompt-evolution and online RL baselines.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; model_type is the controller-assigned type.

rationale: In-scope A-class loop with UCB gate and rollback; strong baselines and 5 seeds, but single replayed task, instance overfitting, table inconsistencies.

sections_read: Appendix A-N (limitations, baselines, complexity, multi-seed, Evolver master prompt, case studies, qwen3 and scaling experiments)

evidence.quote: an evolutionary test-time learning framework that improves an agent without any fine-tuning or gradients—by evolving the entire agentic system after every episode.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: whole-system gradient-free evolution between episodes.

evidence.quote: we find that existing adaptation methods like reflection, memory, or reinforcement learning struggle.
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: existing adapters fail on J-TTL.

evidence.quote: EvoTest generalizes prompt evolution to whole-system evolution, optimizing the entire agentic configuration—including the prompt, memory, hyperparameters, and tool-use routines.
evidence.support_explanation: Delta vs EvoPrompt/Promptbreeder/TextGrad: more channels evolved.

evidence.quote: A system prompt that provides high-level strategic guidance, heuristics, and behavioral guardrails to the backbone LLM.
evidence.support_explanation: Retained object 1: policy prompt.

evidence.quote: Active components executed at each decision-making step to operationalize knowledge and create useful state abstractions.
evidence.support_explanation: Retained object 4: tool-use routines (memory logic + evolvable Python state extractor).

evidence.quote: It also identifies sequences of interactions that led to no progress and records them in a "failure" table.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory update by the Evolver from the transcript.

evidence.quote: At the start of each new episode, the UCB algorithm selects a single configuration, which is then used for the entire duration of that episode.
evidence.support_explanation: Selection rule: UCB over parent+children, scored by one-episode returns.

evidence.quote: The UCB rule can then naturally "fall back" to the time-tested parent, which retains its high score.
evidence.support_explanation: Rollback mechanism: parent stays in pool.

evidence.quote: This ensures that any performance improvement is solely attributable to the agent's internal learning process.
evidence.support_explanation: Same game reset to identical initial state every episode.

evidence.quote: All methods are evaluated under the same step budget and use the same backbone LLMs for their respective roles to ensure a fair comparison.
evidence.support_explanation: Budget-matched in steps; Evolver compute not matched explicitly.

evidence.quote: EvoTest achieves the highest AUC score on all six games, with an average score of 0.47/0.50

signatures.operation: Evolver (o3) rewrites prompt, appends state-action successes to memory, tunes temperature, rewrites extractor/memory-use rule, producing children
signatures.conditions: After every episode of a 50-episode session
signatures.selection_rule: UCB over parent+children using mean episode score
signatures.persistence: Configuration carried to next episode within a session; parent kept in pool
signatures.later_use: Next episodes run with the selected config
signatures.claimed_effect: AUC 0.47/0.50 vs 0.34/0.36 best baseline; wins Detective and Library

gap.author_gap: Agents cannot learn complex skills on the fly; reflection/memory/RL adapt only one channel or lack credit assignment in sparse reward.
gap.checked_gap: Reasonable: prompt-only evolvers leave decoding and memory-use logic fixed; ablation shows non-prompt channels add measurable but smaller gains.
gap.closest_adjacent: EvoPrompt/Promptbreeder (population of prompts), Reflexion; EvoAgent/MASS cited but not compared
gap.residue: Whether gains come from multi-channel evolution or from the engineered Evolver prompt
gap.remaining_gap: Generalization beyond replayed instance; cost of strong Evolver
unresolved: ADAS/AFlow/ExpeL full text not in package

claims.text: EvoTest yields steeper and higher within-session learning than reflection, memory, prompt-optimization and online fine-tuning baselines.
claims.setting: Six Jericho games, 50 episodes, T=110, gemini-2.5-flash/claude-4-sonnet actors, o3 Evolver
claims.baseline_control: Static, Memory, RAG, Summary, Reflexion, TextGrad, Promptbreeder, EvoPrompt, SFT, GRPO
claims.selection_vs_test: Online: UCB uses the same episodes that are scored; identical task replayed
claims.result_denominator: AUC normalized by max score; 5 seeds mean+-std (Table 8); all episodes counted
claims.allowed_conclusion: On repeated replay of the same six games, EvoTest's retained configuration raises later-episode score more than the tested baselines; not shown for task variants or with matched optimizer cost.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Within-session, the evolved configuration (esp. prompt walkthrough) is retained and raises later episode scores on identical replays of six games.

G.reason: Concrete gap: single-channel adaptation (prompt-only, memory-only) and sparse-reward RL fail within-session; neighbors Reflexion/EvoPrompt/Promptbreeder/TextGrad/MemGPT named; missing ADAS/AFlow-style whole-system search and ExpeL-type memory neighbors.

M.reason: Transcript-narrative credit assignment + multi-channel edits + UCB with parent fallback gives distinguishable predictions (stability, ablations), though why four channels jointly is argued by example.

X.reason: Config tuple, Evolver master prompt, selection rule, rollback via parent pool all reconstructable; beta and m deferred to code, memory growth/staleness and execution safety of evolved Python not treated, Sec 4.2 vs App J.2 inconsistency on failure memory.

E.measurement.reason: Native game score from a deterministic engine, normalized AUC; trustworthy verifier, but Table 1 vs Table 8 numbers conflict.

E.causality.reason: Eight literature baselines, five component ablations, Evolver-LLM and structured-prompt ablations, same-backbone GRPO/SFT comparison; ablations on 3 of 6 games, Evolver (o3) stronger than baseline optimizers' unspecified model, gain partly attributable to Evolver prompt engineering.

E.holdout.reason: Same game from identical reset every episode; no held-out variants or contamination check against public Jericho walkthroughs; scope honestly single-task.

E.statistics.reason: 5-seed mean+-std for main table; ablations and cost without variance, no significance tests, conflicting numbers across tables.

E.cost.reason: Per-update wall-time table and complexity analysis vs weight update, but no dollar/token cost of o3 Evolver or children count; search cost partially accounted.
